messages:
sam: Quick heads-up — we're planning a targeted maintenance in az23 this Thu 02:00 UTC to address intermittent BMC flaps that cause NIC resets on ~6 nodes. Will do a soft-evac + BMC handshake, then a staged GPU reboot.
julia: OK — how many racks / how long per rack? any customer-visible impact?
sam: 3 racks total. We'll cordon/drain one rack at a time, ~45m per rack including preheat/backfill checks. No planned customer-facing downtime, but tail latency could spike briefly for high-concurrency tenants.
kevin: Are we doing canaries first? last time one rack showed unexpected NVMe IO wait after reboot.
sam: Yes — canary set: rack-az23-can1 (2 nodes) first. If canary passes 30m of health checks (throughput, nvlink, avg p95 < 200ms) we continue. If not, rollback and escalate.
infra-bot: Deploy window created: 2026-03-26T02:00Z -> 2026-03-26T05:00Z. Playbook: infra/ops/bmc-handshake-2026.md.
julia: Command snippets for the oncall? paste below so SRE can follow.
sam: Sure, basic flow: cordon -> drain soft -> run bmc-handshake -> reboot gpu -> uncordon.
```
# cordon the rack nodes
for n in $(rackctl list --rack rack-az23-7); do kubectl cordon $n; done
# soft drain (allow eviction, don't delete local state)
for n in $(rackctl list --rack rack-az23-7); do kubectl drain $n --ignore-daemonsets --pod-selector='app!=stateful' --delete-emptydir-data=false; done
# trigger BMC handshake
rackctl bmc-handshake --rack rack-az23-7 --confirm
```
kevin: Make sure to set cache-seed on a couple standby nodes before we start the rack drain to reduce prefix penalties.
sam: Good call. We'll seed two standby instances in az23 and az24. Also will enable kv-cache warmup flag for the canary window.
julia: Any cost implications for the backfill capacity? we might spin up burst GPUs for ~90m.
sam: Estimate ~8 extra GPU-hours total -> ~$120 for the window. I've added note to billing leads. Not material but FYI.
oncall-rotation: Oncall for Thu night: kevin. kevin please ack and confirm you'll be available.
kevin: Acked. I'll be online and will watch the canary health dashboard. If p95 > 300ms or NVME errors > 0.5% in canary, I will abort.
sam: Plan to post status in #eng-infra and ping @customer-impact if we see degraded SLOs. Also hooking in trace sampling at 5x for 20 minutes around each reboot step.
julia: Sounds good. Leave a 30m buffer between racks so autoscaler can stabilize.
sam: Done. I'll post the final schedule + JSON playbook to the incident channel an hour prior. :thumbsup:
